Add the green beans, salt and pepper and toss 2 to 3 minutes until heated through.
Stir in 1 tablespoon lemon juice and a little grated zest and serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Green Beans
recipes.description: Green beans roasted at high heat with olive oil and garlic until tender and lightly blistered.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Trim the green beans and pat dry. Toss on a rimmed baking sheet with the olive oil, salt and pepper and spread in a single layer.
Roast 10 minutes. Add the thinly sliced garlic, toss and roast 6 to 8 minutes more until the beans are tender and browned in spots.
Sprinkle with Parmesan and a squeeze of lemon if using and serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
recipes.description: Halved Brussels sprouts roasted cut side down until caramelized, with an optional balsamic drizzle.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the center.
Trim the stem ends of the Brussels sprouts, pull off any yellow outer leaves and halve them lengthwise.
Toss with the olive oil, salt and pepper on a rimmed baking sheet, then turn each sprout cut side down.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes, without stirring, until the cut sides are deep brown and the sprouts are tender when pierced.
Transfer to a bowl, drizzle with balsamic vinegar if using and serve.

recipes.title: Glazed Carrots
recipes.description: Tender carrots finished in a buttery brown sugar and honey glaze.
steps: Peel the carrots and slice them on the diagonal 1/4 inch thick.
Cover with salted water in a large skillet, bring to a boil and simmer 6 to 8 minutes until just tender. Drain and wipe out the skillet.
Melt the butter in the skillet over medium heat and stir in the brown sugar, honey, salt and pepper until the sugar dissolves.
Add the carrots and cook, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes until they are coated in a glossy glaze.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley if using and serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Vegetables
recipes.description: A sheet pan of zucchini, squash, peppers, onion, broccoli and carrots roasted with olive oil and Italian herbs.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment.
Cut the zucchini, squash, bell pepper and onion into 1-inch pieces, cut the broccoli into florets and slice the carrots 1/4 inch thick so they cook as fast as the rest.
Toss all the vegetables with the olive oil, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Spread in a single layer across both pans without crowding.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once halfway, until tender and browned at the edges.
Drizzle with balsamic vinegar if using and serve.

recipes.title: Creamed Corn
recipes.description: Sweet corn simmered in a rich butter, cream and cream cheese sauce.
steps: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the corn and cook 4 to 5 minutes until thawed and hot.
Whisk the cornstarch into the milk until smooth.
Add the cream, cream cheese, sugar, salt and pepper to the corn and stir until the cream cheese melts.
Stir in the milk mixture and simmer, stirring often, 4 to 5 minutes until thick and creamy.
For a creamier texture, purée about 1 cup of the corn with an immersion blender and stir it back in. Stir in Parmesan if using and serve.

recipes.title: Creamed Spinach
recipes.description: Steakhouse-style creamed spinach with shallot, garlic, cream cheese, Parmesan and a pinch of nutmeg.
steps: Thaw the spinach and squeeze it firmly in a clean kitchen towel to remove as much liquid as possible.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the minced shallot 2 minutes, then add the minced garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add the cream cheese and cream and stir until smooth and simmering.
Stir in the spinach, Parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper and cook 3 to 4 minutes until thick and heated through.
Taste for seasoning and serve hot.

recipes.title: Garlic Parmesan Broccoli
recipes.description: Broccoli florets roasted with garlic and olive oil and finished with Parmesan and lemon.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Cut the broccoli into bite-size florets and pat dry.
Toss with the olive oil, minced garlic, salt, pepper and red pepper flakes if using, and spread in a single layer.
Roast 12 minutes, then sprinkle with the Parmesan and roast 4 to 6 minutes more until the florets are tender with browned edges.
Squeeze lemon over the top if using and serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Asparagus
recipes.description: Asparagus spears roasted with olive oil and garlic and brightened with fresh lemon.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Snap or trim the woody ends off the asparagus.
Toss the spears on a rimmed baking sheet with the olive oil, minced garlic, salt and pepper and spread in a single layer.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes for medium spears (8 for thin, up to 15 for thick) until tender-crisp and lightly browned.
Grate a little lemon zest over the top, squeeze on some juice and sprinkle with Parmesan if using. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Fried Okra
recipes.description: Southern-style okra soaked in buttermilk, dredged in seasoned cornmeal and pan-fried until golden and crunchy.
steps: Trim the stem ends of the okra and slice into 1/2-inch rounds. Soak in the buttermilk for 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk the cornmeal, flour, 3/4 teaspoon salt, pepper, garlic powder and cayenne.
Heat the oil (about 1/2 inch deep) in a 10-inch cast-iron skillet or heavy pot to 350°F.
Lift the okra from the buttermilk with a slotted spoon, letting excess drip off, and toss in the cornmeal mixture to coat completely.
Fry in batches, without crowding, for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on a paper towel-lined plate, sprinkle with the remaining salt and serve hot.

recipes.title: Homemade Dinner Rolls
recipes.description: Soft, fluffy yeast rolls made with milk, butter and a little sugar, baked together in a pan and brushed with butter.
steps: Warm the milk to 110°F. Stir in 1 tablespoon of the sugar and the yeast and let stand 5 to 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl or stand mixer, combine the yeast mixture, remaining sugar, 4 tablespoons softened butter, the egg and the salt. Add 3 1/2 cups flour and mix until a soft dough forms.
Knead 6 to 8 minutes by hand (5 minutes with a dough hook), adding up to 1/4 cup more flour as needed, until smooth, elastic and only slightly tacky.
Place in a greased bowl, cover and let rise in a warm spot 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Punch down the dough, divide into 16 equal pieces and roll each into a smooth ball. Arrange in a greased 9x13-inch pan, cover and let rise 45 minutes, until puffy and touching.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until golden brown on top and the centers register 190°F.
Brush with the remaining tablespoon of melted butter and serve warm.

recipes.title: Garlic Knots
recipes.description: Store-bought pizza dough tied into knots, baked golden and brushed with garlic butter, herbs and Parmesan.
steps: Let the dough sit at room temperature for 30 minutes so it is easier to stretch. Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
On a lightly floured surface, divide the dough into 16 pieces. Roll each into a 7-inch rope and tie it in a loose knot, tucking the ends underneath.
Arrange the knots 2 inches apart on the baking sheet and bake 13 to 16 minutes, until golden brown.
Meanwhile, melt the butter with the olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add the minced garlic, Italian seasoning and salt and cook 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Brush the hot knots generously with the garlic butter, then sprinkle with chopped parsley and Parmesan.
Serve warm with warmed marinara for dipping if desired.

recipes.title: Cheddar Bay Biscuits
recipes.description: Garlicky drop biscuits loaded with sharp cheddar and brushed with parsley-garlic butter, in the style of the famous seafood-restaurant biscuits.
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, 1 teaspoon garlic powder and the salt in a large bowl. Stir in the shredded cheddar.
Melt 8 tablespoons of the butter and let it cool slightly. Stir it into the cold buttermilk (it will clump; that's fine).
Pour the buttermilk mixture into the dry ingredients and stir just until no dry flour remains.
Scoop the dough into 12 mounds (about 1/4 cup each) on the baking sheet. Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until golden brown.
Melt the remaining 3 tablespoons butter with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder and the chopped parsley. Brush over the hot biscuits and serve warm.

recipes.title: Homemade Cornbread
recipes.description: Moist, lightly sweet buttermilk cornbread with a golden crust, baked in an 8-inch pan or cast-iron skillet.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Grease an 8x8-inch baking pan or 9-inch cast-iron skillet.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Melt the butter. In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk and eggs, then whisk in the melted butter.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir just until combined; a few lumps are fine.
Spread in the pan and bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the top is golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes, then cut into 9 squares or wedges and serve warm.

recipes.title: Monkey Bread
recipes.description: Pull-apart cinnamon-sugar bread made from refrigerated biscuit dough baked in a Bundt pan with a buttery caramel glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and generously grease a 10- or 12-cup Bundt pan.
Mix the granulated sugar and cinnamon in a large zip-top bag.
Cut each biscuit into quarters. Shake the pieces in the cinnamon sugar, about 8 at a time, until coated, and layer them in the pan, scattering chopped pecans between layers if using.
Melt the butter with the brown sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring, until it just comes to a boil. Remove from the heat, stir in the vanilla and pour evenly over the dough.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until deep golden and the dough in the center is no longer doughy.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a plate. Serve warm, pulling the pieces apart.

recipes.title: Blueberry Muffins
recipes.description: Tender, buttery muffins packed with fresh blueberries and topped with a sprinkle of sugar.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the flour, 3/4 cup sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Toss the blueberries with 1 tablespoon of the flour mixture.
Melt the butter and let it cool slightly. Whisk it with the eggs, milk and vanilla.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry just until combined, then gently fold in the blueberries.
Divide the batter among the cups and sprinkle the tops with the extra sugar if using.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then move to a rack.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Muffins
recipes.description: Bakery-style muffins made tender with sour cream and studded with semi-sweet chocolate chips.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs, sour cream, milk, oil and vanilla until smooth.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry just until combined, then fold in all but 2 tablespoons of the chocolate chips.
Fill the muffin cups nearly to the top and scatter the reserved chips over the batter.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until domed and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with only melted chocolate, not wet batter. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then move to a rack.

recipes.title: Bran Muffins
recipes.description: Moist, hearty bran muffins sweetened with brown sugar and molasses and dotted with raisins.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease or line a 12-cup muffin pan.
Stir the wheat bran into the buttermilk and let it soak for 10 minutes.
Whisk the oil, egg, brown sugar, molasses and vanilla, then stir in the bran mixture.
In a separate bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon.
Add the dry ingredients to the bran mixture and stir just until combined. Fold in the raisins.
Divide among the muffin cups and bake 15 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan before removing.

recipes.title: French Toast Casserole
recipes.description: Cubed French bread soaked overnight in a cinnamon-vanilla custard and baked under a brown sugar crumb topping.
steps: Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Cut the bread into 1-inch cubes (day-old bread works best) and spread them in the dish.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, 1/4 cup brown sugar, vanilla, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, the nutmeg and salt. Pour evenly over the bread and press the cubes down to soak.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight.
For the topping, mix the flour, remaining 1/2 cup brown sugar and remaining 1 teaspoon cinnamon, then cut in the cold butter until crumbly. Refrigerate until baking.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Take the casserole out of the refrigerator while the oven heats and sprinkle the topping over it.
Bake uncovered 45 to 50 minutes, until puffed and golden and the center is set (160°F). Tent with foil if the top browns too fast.
Rest 10 minutes, then dust with powdered sugar and serve with maple syrup if desired.

recipes.title: Breakfast Hash
recipes.description: Crispy diced potatoes cooked with bacon, onion and bell peppers, topped with eggs cooked right in the skillet.
steps: Scrub the potatoes and cut into 1/2-inch cubes. Dice the onion and both bell peppers, and mince the garlic.
Cook the bacon in a large cast-iron or nonstick skillet over medium heat until crisp, 6 to 8 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate, leaving the drippings in the pan, then crumble once cool.

Add the oil to the drippings, then add the potatoes in an even layer. Cook without stirring for 5 minutes, then stir and continue cooking, stirring every few minutes, until browned and nearly tender, about 10 minutes more.
Add the onion and bell peppers and cook until softened and the potatoes are fork-tender, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, paprika, salt and pepper and cook 1 minute.
Stir the bacon back in. Make 4 wells in the hash and crack an egg into each.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover and cook until the whites are set and the yolks are done to your liking, 4 to 6 minutes.
Sprinkle with green onions, if using, and serve straight from the skillet.

recipes.title: Sausage Hash
recipes.description: Breakfast sausage, potatoes, onion and green pepper browned together in one skillet and finished with melted cheddar.
steps: Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes, dice the onion and bell pepper, and shred the cheddar.
Put the potatoes in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of water, cover and microwave on high for 5 minutes until just tender; drain well.
Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into crumbles, until no pink remains, 7 to 8 minutes. Transfer to a bowl with a slotted spoon.
Add the oil to the skillet, then the potatoes in a single layer. Cook undisturbed for 4 minutes, then stir and cook until golden and crisp on several sides, about 8 minutes more.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Season with the garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt and pepper.
Return the sausage to the skillet and stir to combine. Scatter the cheddar over the top, cover and cook 1 to 2 minutes until melted.
If you like, fry the eggs in a separate pan and set one on each serving. Garnish with green onions and serve hot.

recipes.title: Egg & Cheese Breakfast Burritos
recipes.description: Soft scrambled eggs and melted cheddar rolled in warm flour tortillas, with salsa on the side.
steps: Shred the cheddar. Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in a bowl until no streaks of white remain.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 20 seconds per side, then wrap them in a clean towel to keep soft.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the eggs and cook, stirring slowly with a spatula, until softly set but still moist, 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Divide the eggs among the tortillas, placing them just below center, and top each with a quarter of the cheddar and some green onions, if using.
Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly from the bottom.
Place the burritos seam side down in the skillet over medium heat and toast 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden and the cheese is melted. Serve with salsa.

recipes.title: Breakfast Pizza
recipes.description: A homemade pizza crust topped with breakfast sausage, soft scrambled eggs and two cheeses.
steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into 1 cup of warm water (about 110°F) and let stand until foamy, 5 minutes. Add the flour, salt and 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and stir into a shaggy dough.
Knead on a lightly floured counter until smooth and elastic, about 6 minutes. Place in an oiled bowl, cover and let rise in a warm spot until doubled, about 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 450°F. Brush a large rimmed baking sheet with the remaining olive oil. Press and stretch the dough to fill the pan and let it rest 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, brown the sausage in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains, about 7 minutes. Drain on paper towels.

Whisk the eggs with the milk. Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and cook the eggs, stirring gently, until barely set and still glossy, about 2 minutes. They will finish in the oven.
Bake the plain crust for 6 minutes. Shred the cheddar.
Top the crust with half the mozzarella, then the eggs, sausage, cheddar and remaining mozzarella.
Bake until the crust is golden underneath and the cheese is bubbling, 8 to 10 minutes. Sprinkle with green onions, if using, and cut into squares.

recipes.title: Breakfast Tacos
recipes.description: Warm corn tortillas filled with scrambled eggs, crispy potatoes, bacon and cheddar, topped with salsa.
steps: Peel the potato and cut into 1/4-inch dice. Shred the cheddar.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp, 6 to 8 minutes. Drain on paper towels and crumble, leaving about 2 tablespoons of drippings in the pan.
Add the potato to the drippings with 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and tender, 10 to 12 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining salt and the pepper. Reduce the heat to medium-low, pour the eggs over the potatoes and cook, stirring gently, until just set, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in the bacon.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame for about 30 seconds per side, then wrap in a towel.
Fill each tortilla with the egg mixture and top with cheddar, salsa, and sliced avocado and cilantro if using.

recipes.title: Egg Muffins
recipes.description: Make-ahead baked eggs with ham, spinach, red pepper and cheddar, cooked in a muffin tin.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and brush a 12-cup muffin tin generously with the oil.
Dice the ham and bell pepper, chop the spinach, slice the green onions and shred the cheddar.
Divide the ham, spinach, bell pepper, green onions and cheddar evenly among the muffin cups.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper together until smooth, then pour over the fillings, filling each cup about three-quarters full.
Bake until puffed and set in the center, 20 to 22 minutes; a knife inserted in the center should come out clean.
Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then run a thin knife around each muffin and lift out. Refrigerate leftovers up to 4 days and reheat in the microwave for 30 to 45 seconds.

recipes.title: Oatmeal
recipes.description: Creamy stovetop rolled oats cooked in milk and water, sweetened with brown sugar and cinnamon.
steps: Bring the milk, 1 cup of water and the salt to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium heat, watching so the milk does not boil over.
Stir in the oats and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in the cinnamon and let stand 1 minute to thicken.
Spoon into bowls and top with the brown sugar, plus sliced banana and chopped walnuts if using.

recipes.title: Overnight Oats
recipes.description: No-cook rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and yogurt, lightly sweetened with maple syrup and topped with blueberries.
steps: In a bowl or quart jar, stir together the oats, milk, yogurt, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until evenly combined.
Divide between two jars or containers with lids.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight, until the oats are soft and have absorbed most of the liquid.
In the morning, stir, adding a splash of milk if it is too thick, and top with the blueberries and chopped almonds, if using. Eat cold or microwave for 1 minute.

recipes.title: Granola
recipes.description: Crunchy oven-baked oat granola with almonds, pecans and dried cranberries, sweetened with maple syrup.
steps: Heat the oven to 300°F and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Coarsely chop the almonds and pecans. In a large bowl, combine the oats, nuts, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Melt the coconut oil and whisk it with the maple syrup and vanilla. Pour over the oat mixture and stir until everything is evenly coated.
Spread the mixture in an even layer on the baking sheet and press it down lightly with a spatula.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through, until golden brown. Stir only once if you want large clusters.
Let cool completely on the pan without stirring; it crisps as it cools. Break into clusters and stir in the dried cranberries.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Breakfast Parfait
recipes.description: Layers of Greek yogurt, fresh berries and crunchy granola drizzled with honey.
steps: Hull and slice the strawberries and rinse the blueberries.
Stir half of the honey into the yogurt.
In two glasses or jars, layer a quarter of the yogurt, a quarter of the fruit and 2 tablespoons of granola. Repeat the layers once more.
Drizzle with the remaining honey and serve right away so the granola stays crunchy.

recipes.title: Stuffed Mushrooms
recipes.description: Mushroom caps filled with a garlicky cream cheese, Parmesan and breadcrumb stuffing and baked until golden.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a rimmed baking sheet. Soften the cream cheese at room temperature.
Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp paper towel (choose about 24 large ones). Pop out the stems and finely chop them; arrange the caps hollow side up on the baking sheet.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped stems and cook until their liquid evaporates, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook 30 seconds, then let cool slightly.
In a bowl, mix the cream cheese, all but 2 tablespoons of the Parmesan, the breadcrumbs, Italian seasoning, salt, pepper and the cooked stems.
Spoon the filling into the caps, mounding it slightly, and sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan.
Bake until the mushrooms are tender and the tops are golden, 20 to 25 minutes.
Let cool 5 minutes, sprinkle with chopped parsley if using, and serve warm.

recipes.title: Cheese Ball
recipes.description: A make-ahead cheddar and cream cheese ball rolled in chopped pecans, served with crackers.
steps: Let the cream cheese soften at room temperature for about 30 minutes. Finely shred the cheddar and thinly slice the green onions.
Beat the cream cheese in a bowl with a spoon or mixer until smooth. Add the cheddar, green onions, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder and pepper and mix until evenly combined.
Scrape the mixture onto a sheet of plastic wrap, shape it into a ball, wrap tightly and refrigerate until firm, at least 2 hours or up to 2 days.
Finely chop the pecans and mix with the chopped parsley, if using, on a plate.
Unwrap the cheese ball and roll it in the pecan mixture, pressing gently so the nuts stick on all sides.
Let stand 15 minutes at room temperature before serving with crackers.

recipes.title: Homemade Hummus
recipes.description: Smooth, creamy chickpea hummus blended with tahini, lemon and garlic.
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Juice the lemon; you need about 3 tablespoons.
In a food processor, blend the tahini and lemon juice for 1 minute until thick and creamy, scraping the bowl once.
Add the garlic, 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the cumin and salt and blend 30 seconds.
Add the chickpeas and process for 2 minutes. With the motor running, drizzle in 2 to 4 tablespoons of ice water until the hummus is very smooth and fluffy.
Taste and add more salt or lemon juice if needed.
Spread in a shallow bowl, make a swirl with the back of a spoon, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and sprinkle with paprika and parsley, if using. Refrigerate leftovers up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Hummus & Vegetables
recipes.description: A bowl of homemade hummus served with a platter of fresh-cut vegetables for dipping.
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas and juice the lemon.
In a food processor, blend the tahini and 3 tablespoons of lemon juice until creamy, about 1 minute. Add the garlic, 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the cumin and salt and blend again.
Add the chickpeas and process for 2 minutes, drizzling in 2 to 4 tablespoons of ice water until smooth. Season to taste with more salt or lemon.
Peel the carrots and cut into sticks. Slice the cucumber into rounds, cut the bell pepper into strips, cut the celery into sticks and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Spoon the hummus into a bowl, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and sprinkle with paprika, if using.
Set the bowl on a platter, arrange the vegetables around it and serve, or pack into containers for lunches.

recipes.title: Cucumber Bites
recipes.description: Crisp cucumber rounds topped with a ranch-seasoned cream cheese spread and a cherry tomato half.
steps: Soften the cream cheese at room temperature for 20 to 30 minutes.
Stir the cream cheese, sour cream and ranch seasoning together until smooth.
Slice the cucumbers into 1/4-inch-thick rounds (about 32) and pat dry with paper towels.
Spoon or pipe about 1 1/2 teaspoons of the spread onto each cucumber round.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and press one half onto each bite. Sprinkle with sliced green onions, if using.
Serve right away, or refrigerate up to 2 hours before serving.

recipes.title: Caprese Skewers
recipes.description: Cherry tomatoes, fresh mozzarella and basil threaded on skewers and drizzled with olive oil and a quick balsamic glaze.
steps: Simmer the balsamic vinegar in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until reduced to about 3 tablespoons and syrupy, 8 to 10 minutes. Let cool; it thickens as it cools.
Drain the mozzarella pearls and pat dry. Pick about 24 small basil leaves.
On each of 24 short skewers or toothpicks, thread a cherry tomato, a folded basil leaf and a mozzarella pearl.
Arrange on a platter, drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Drizzle with the balsamic glaze just before serving.

recipes.title: Antipasto Skewers
recipes.description: Bite-size skewers of salami, fresh mozzarella, cherry tomatoes and olives tossed in a quick Italian vinaigrette.
steps: Whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar, Italian seasoning, red pepper flakes and black pepper in a bowl.
Drain the mozzarella pearls, add to the vinaigrette and toss. Let marinate 10 minutes.
Fold each salami slice in half and then in half again.
On each of 24 short skewers, thread a cherry tomato, a folded salami slice, a mozzarella pearl, a basil leaf if using, and an olive.
Arrange on a platter and drizzle with any vinaigrette left in the bowl. Serve right away or refrigerate up to 4 hours.

recipes.title: Fried Pickles
recipes.description: Dill pickle chips dipped in buttermilk and a seasoned flour and cornmeal coating, fried crisp and served with a ranch dip.
steps: Stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream and ranch seasoning with 1 tablespoon of water and refrigerate while you fry.
Drain the pickle chips and pat them very dry with paper towels.
Whisk the buttermilk and egg in a bowl. In a second bowl, whisk the flour, cornmeal, paprika, garlic powder, cayenne and salt.
Heat the oil in a heavy 3- to 4-quart pot or Dutch oven to 375°F; it should be at least 1 1/2 inches deep.
Working with a handful at a time, dip the pickles in the buttermilk mixture, let the excess drip off, then toss in the flour mixture to coat.
Fry in small batches without crowding, turning once, until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Let the oil return to 375°F between batches.
Drain on a rack set over paper towels and serve hot with the ranch dip.

recipes.title: Onion Rings
recipes.description: Thick-cut onion rings dipped in buttermilk, coated in seasoned flour and panko, and fried until crunchy.
steps: Peel the onions and slice crosswise into 1/2-inch rounds, then separate into rings. Save the tiny center pieces for another use.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, paprika and 3/4 teaspoon of the salt in a shallow dish. In a second dish, whisk the buttermilk and egg. Put the panko in a third dish.
Heat the oil in a heavy 3- to 4-quart pot or Dutch oven to 375°F; it should be at least 1 1/2 inches deep. Set a wire rack over a sheet pan.
Dredge each ring in the flour, dip in the buttermilk mixture, then press into the panko to coat completely. Set on the rack.
Fry a few rings at a time, turning once, until deep golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Let the oil come back to 375°F between batches.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with the remaining salt while hot and serve immediately with ketchup or your favorite dip.

recipes.title: Potato Wedges with Dip
recipes.description: Oven-roasted seasoned russet potato wedges served with a creamy ranch-style sour cream dip.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Scrub the potatoes and cut each lengthwise into 8 wedges. Soak in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat very dry.
Toss the wedges with the olive oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt and pepper and arrange cut side down in a single layer.
Roast for 20 minutes, flip the wedges, and roast until golden and tender in the center, 15 to 20 minutes more.
While the potatoes roast, stir together the sour cream, mayonnaise, ranch seasoning and sliced green onions. Refrigerate until serving.
Sprinkle the hot wedges with Parmesan, if using, and serve with the dip.

recipes.title: Corn Dip
recipes.description: A warm, cheesy baked corn dip with cream cheese, cheddar, jalapeño and green onions, served with tortilla chips.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Soften the cream cheese, shred the cheddar, seed and mince the jalapeño and slice the green onions.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the corn and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly charred in spots, 6 to 8 minutes. Let cool slightly.
In a bowl, mix the cream cheese, sour cream and mayonnaise until smooth. Stir in the corn, two-thirds of the cheddar, the jalapeño, most of the green onions, the chili powder, garlic powder and salt.
Spread in a 2-quart baking dish or 9-inch deep-dish pie plate and top with the remaining cheddar.
Bake until bubbling at the edges and the cheese is melted, 20 to 25 minutes.
Sprinkle with the remaining green onions and serve warm with tortilla chips.

recipes.title: Warm Crab Dip
recipes.description: Lump crab baked in a creamy, lemony cream cheese base with a melted mozzarella top, served with crackers.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and soften the cream cheese at room temperature.
Pick through the crab for any bits of shell, keeping the lumps as intact as possible.

In a bowl, beat the cream cheese, sour cream and mayonnaise until smooth. Mix in the Parmesan, 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon, minced garlic, half the paprika, the hot sauce and most of the sliced green onions.
Gently fold in the crab.
Spread in a small baking dish or 9-inch pie plate, top with the mozzarella and sprinkle with the remaining paprika.
Bake until bubbling and golden on top, 20 to 25 minutes.
Garnish with the remaining green onions and serve warm with crackers.

recipes.title: Ranch Pretzel Bites
recipes.description: Mini pretzels tossed in oil and ranch seasoning and baked low until the coating sets.
steps: Heat the oven to 250°F and line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk the oil, ranch seasoning, garlic powder and onion powder.
Add the pretzels and stir for a minute or two until every piece is coated.
Spread on the baking sheets in a single layer.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the coating looks dry and the pretzels are fragrant.
Cool completely on the pans, then store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Mini Quiches
recipes.description: Bite-size quiches with bacon, cheddar and green onion baked in pie crust in a mini muffin pan.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a 24-cup mini muffin pan.
Unroll the pie crusts and cut out 24 rounds with a 2 1/2-inch cutter, re-rolling scraps as needed. Press a round into each cup.
Cook the bacon until crisp, drain on paper towels and finely crumble. Shred the cheddar and slice the green onions.
Divide the bacon, cheddar and green onions among the crusts.
Whisk the eggs, half and half, salt, pepper and nutmeg, and spoon about 1 tablespoon into each cup, filling almost to the top.
Bake until the filling is puffed and set and the crust is golden, 18 to 22 minutes.
Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then lift out with a small knife. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Sausage Balls
recipes.description: Classic bite-size sausage and cheddar balls made with a from-scratch biscuit mix and baked until browned.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, garlic powder and cayenne in a large bowl. Cut the cold butter into small pieces and rub it into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Finely shred the cheddar. Add the raw sausage, cheddar and milk to the bowl and mix with your hands until evenly combined.
Roll into 1-inch balls (about 48) and set 1 inch apart on the baking sheets.
Bake until browned and cooked through, 18 to 22 minutes, rotating the pans halfway; the centers should reach 160°F.
Cool 5 minutes on the pans and serve warm. Baked balls can be refrigerated for 4 days or frozen up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Puppy Chow
recipes.description: Crispy rice cereal squares coated in melted chocolate and peanut butter, then tossed in powdered sugar.
steps: Measure the cereal into a very large bowl.
Microwave the chocolate chips, peanut butter and butter in a microwave-safe bowl for 1 minute, stir, then heat in 15-second bursts, stirring each time, until smooth. Stir in the vanilla.
Pour the chocolate mixture over the cereal and gently fold with a spatula until every piece is coated.
Sift or sprinkle half of the powdered sugar over the cereal and fold, then add the rest and keep folding until the pieces are fully coated and no longer sticky.
Spread on a sheet of wax paper to cool and set, about 15 minutes.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Muddy Buddies
recipes.description: The chocolate-peanut butter snack mix made by shaking coated cereal squares with powdered sugar in a bag.
steps: Pour the cereal into a large bowl and set aside.
In a small saucepan over low heat, melt the chocolate chips, peanut butter and butter, stirring constantly, until smooth, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Pour over the cereal, stirring gently until evenly coated.
Put the powdered sugar in a 2-gallon zip-top bag. Add the coated cereal, seal and shake until well coated.
Spread on wax paper to cool completely, about 20 minutes, then store in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Cookies
recipes.description: Soft, chewy peanut butter cookies with the classic crisscross fork pattern on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. Soften the butter.
Beat the butter, peanut butter, granulated sugar and brown sugar until light and creamy, about 2 minutes. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt, then mix into the peanut butter mixture on low speed just until combined.
Roll the dough into 1 1/2-inch balls (about 2 tablespoons each) and place 2 inches apart on the baking sheets. Flatten each with a fork, pressing once in each direction to make a crisscross.
Bake until the edges are just set and lightly golden but the centers still look soft, 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool on the pans 5 minutes, then move to a rack to cool completely.

recipes.title: Sugar Cookies
recipes.description: Rolled and cut-out butter sugar cookies with a simple glaze icing that sets firm for decorating.
steps: Soften the butter. Beat the butter and granulated sugar until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the egg, vanilla and almond extract, if using.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then mix into the butter mixture on low speed until a soft dough forms.
Divide the dough in half, flatten into disks, wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment paper. Roll each disk 1/4 inch thick on a floured counter and cut into shapes, re-rolling scraps once.
Bake 1 inch apart until the edges are set but not browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Cool on the pan 5 minutes, then on a rack until completely cool.
For the icing, whisk the powdered sugar, milk and corn syrup until smooth and thick enough to drizzle, adding milk by the 1/2 teaspoon if needed.
Spread or pipe the icing onto the cookies and let set at room temperature for 2 to 4 hours before stacking.

recipes.title: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
recipes.description: Chewy brown sugar oatmeal cookies with raisins and a hint of cinnamon.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. Soften the butter.
Beat the butter, brown sugar and granulated sugar until creamy, about 2 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt, and mix into the butter mixture on low speed just until combined.
Stir in the oats and raisins.
Scoop rounded 2-tablespoon portions of dough 2 inches apart onto the baking sheets.
Bake until the edges are golden but the centers still look slightly underdone, 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool on the pans 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

recipes.title: Snickerdoodles
recipes.description: Soft, tangy butter cookies rolled in cinnamon sugar before baking.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. Soften the butter.
Beat the butter with 1 1/2 cups of the sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt, and mix into the butter mixture on low speed until combined.
Stir the remaining 1/4 cup sugar and the cinnamon together in a small bowl.
Roll the dough into 1 1/2-inch balls, roll each in the cinnamon sugar and place 2 inches apart on the baking sheets.
Bake until set at the edges with crackly tops but still soft in the center, 8 to 10 minutes.
Cool on the pans 2 minutes, then move to a rack to cool completely.

recipes.title: Chocolate Fudge
recipes.description: Easy, rich chocolate fudge made with sweetened condensed milk and chocolate chips, no candy thermometer needed.
steps: Line an 8-by-8-inch pan with parchment paper or foil, leaving an overhang on two sides.
Combine the chocolate chips, sweetened condensed milk and butter in a heavy saucepan over low heat. Stir constantly until the chocolate is melted and the mixture is smooth, 4 to 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla, salt and chopped walnuts, if using.
Spread evenly in the pan and smooth the top.
Refrigerate until firm, at least 2 hours.
Lift out using the overhang and cut into 36 squares. Store covered in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Blueberry Pie
recipes.description: A double-crust pie filled with fresh blueberries, lemon and a touch of cinnamon, baked until thick and bubbling.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the lower third. Fit one crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
Zest the lemon and squeeze 1 tablespoon of juice. In a large bowl, gently toss the blueberries with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon zest and juice, cinnamon and salt.
Pour the filling into the crust and dot with small pieces of butter.
Lay the second crust over the top, trim the overhang to 1 inch, fold it under and crimp the edges. Cut 4 or 5 slits in the top for steam.
Beat the egg with 1 tablespoon of water and brush over the top crust. Set the pie on a foil-lined baking sheet.

Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce the heat to 375°F and bake until the crust is deep golden and the filling is bubbling thickly through the slits, 35 to 45 minutes more. Cover the edges with foil if they brown too fast.
Cool on a rack for at least 3 hours so the filling sets before slicing.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pie
recipes.description: Classic spiced pumpkin custard pie with evaporated milk, baked in a flaky crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Fit the crust into a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate and crimp the edges.
In a small bowl, mix the sugar, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, nutmeg and salt.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs, then stir in the pumpkin and the sugar mixture. Gradually whisk in the evaporated milk until smooth.
Pour the filling into the crust and set the pie on a baking sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce the heat to 350°F and bake until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean, 40 to 50 minutes. The center may still jiggle slightly.
Cool on a rack for 2 hours, then serve or refrigerate.
If desired, whip the heavy cream with the powdered sugar to soft peaks and serve with each slice.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Blondies
recipes.description: Chewy brown sugar bars studded with chocolate chips, baked in a 9-by-13-inch pan.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9-by-13-inch pan and line it with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the long sides.
Melt the butter and let it cool for 5 minutes. Whisk in the brown sugar until smooth, then whisk in the eggs and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a separate bowl, then fold into the butter mixture just until no dry flour remains.
Fold in 1 1/4 cups of the chocolate chips. Spread the batter in the pan and scatter the remaining chips on top.
Bake until golden, the edges are set and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs, 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool completely in the pan on a rack, then lift out and cut into 24 bars.
